content.text: # Task: fix a reported bug in `hatetris` ## Bug report (verbatim from the project's issue tracker) **Incomplete replays cause a softlock** If you play a replay that doesn't end the game (for example, `D`), then the game will be stuck in replay mode even after there are no more inputs, forcing the user to refresh the page. This isn't that much of a problem since the game always outputs complete replays, though it should still probably allow the user to do something once the replay ends. Image of replay `D`: ## Standing instructions (identical for every run) You are working in the repository at the current working directory. Work like a careful open-source contributor: 1. Reproduce the bug first (write a minimal failing test or script) before changing code. 2. Find the root cause; fix the cause, not the symptom. Keep the change minimal and in the project's style. 3. Add or update a regression test that fails before your fix and passes after. 4. Run the project's test suite and make it green. Do not modify or delete unrelated tests. 5. When done, summarize: root cause, the files you changed, how you verified it. Do not ask me for permission between steps; proceed until the task is complete, then report. Test command for this repo: `npm run unit`

81:export const getLogic = ({
82:  bar,
83:  rotationSystem,
84:  wellDepth,
85:  wellWidth
86:}: GameProps) => {
87:  /**
88:    Generate a unique integer to describe the position and orientation of this piece.
89:    `x` varies between -3 and (`wellWidth` - 1) inclusive, so range = `wellWidth` + 3
90:    `y` varies between 0 and (`wellDepth` + 2) inclusive, so range = `wellDepth` + 3
91:    `o` varies between 0 and 3 inclusive, so range = 4
92:  */
93:  const getHashCode = (piece: Piece): number =>
94:    (piece.x * (wellDepth + 3) + piece.y) * 4 + piece.o
95:
96:  /**
97:    Input {wellState, piece} and a move, return
98:    the new {wellState, piece}.
99:  */
100:  const getNextState = (wellState: WellState, move: string): WellState => {
101:    let nextWell = wellState.core.well
102:    let nextScore = wellState.core.score
103:    const nextAiState = wellState.ai
104:    const piece = wellState.piece
105:
106:    /* node:coverage disable */
107:    if (piece === null) {
108:      throw Error('Can\'t get next well state if there is no piece in the well')
109:    }
110:    /* node:coverage enable */
111:
112:    let nextPiece: Piece | null = { ...piece }
113:
114:    // apply transform
115:    if (move === 'L') {
116:      nextPiece.x--
117:    }
118:    if (move === 'R') {
119:      nextPiece.x++
120:    }
121:    if (move === 'D') {
122:      nextPiece.y++
123:    }
124:    if (move === 'U') {
125:      nextPiece.o = (nextPiece.o + 1) % 4
126:    }
127:
128:    const orientation = rotationSystem.rotations[nextPiece.id][nextPiece.o]
129:    const xActual = nextPiece.x + orientation.xMin
130:    const yActual = nextPiece.y + orientation.yMin
131:
132:    if (
133:      xActual < 0 || // off left side
134:      xActual + orientation.xDim > wellWidth || // off right side
135:      yActual < 0 || // off top (??)
136:      yActual + orientation.yDim > wellDepth || // off bottom
137:      orientation.rows.some((row, y) =>
138:        wellState.core.well[yActual + y] & (row << xActual)
139:      ) // obstruction
140:    ) {
141:      if (move === 'D') {
142:        // Lock piece
143:        nextWell = wellState.core.well.slice()
144:
145:        const orientation = rotationSystem.rotations[piece.id][piece.o]
146:
147:        // this is the top left point in the bounding box of this orientation of this piece
148:        const xActual = piece.x + orientation.xMin
149:        const yActual = piece.y + orientation.yMin
150:
151:        // row by row bitwise line alteration
152:        for (let row = 0; row < orientation.yDim; row++) {
153:          // can't negative bit-shift, but alas X can be negative
154:          nextWell[yActual + row] |= (orientation.rows[row] << xActual)
155:        }
156:
157:        // check for complete lines now
158:        // NOTE: completed lines don't count if you've lost
159:        for (let row = 0; row < orientation.yDim; row++) {
160:          if (
161:            yActual >= bar &&
162:            nextWell[yActual + row] === (1 << wellWidth) - 1
163:          ) {
164:            // move all lines above this point down
165:            for (let k = yActual + row; k > 1; k--) {
166:              nextWell[k] = nextWell[k - 1]
167:            }
168:
169:            // insert a new blank line at the top
170:            // though of course the top line will always be blank anyway
171:            nextWell[0] = 0
172:
173:            nextScore++
174:          }
175:        }
176:        nextPiece = null
177:      } else {
178:        // No move
179:        nextPiece = piece
180:      }
181:    }
182:
183:    return {
184:      core: {
185:        well: nextWell,
186:        score: nextScore
187:      },
188:      ai: nextAiState,
189:      piece: nextPiece
190:    }
191:  }
192:
193:  /**
194:    Given a well and a piece ID, find all possible places where it could land
195:    and return the array of "possible future" states. All of these states
196:    will have `null` `piece` because the piece is landed; some will have
197:    a positive `score`.
198:  */
199:  const getNextCoreStates = (core: CoreState, pieceId: string): CoreState[] => {
200:    let piece = rotationSystem.placeNewPiece(wellWidth, pieceId)
201:
202:    // move the piece down to a lower position before we have to
203:    // start pathfinding for it
204:    // move through empty rows
205:    while (
206:      piece.y + 4 < wellDepth && // piece is above the bottom
207:      core.well[piece.y + 4] === 0 // nothing immediately below it
208:    ) {
209:      const nextPiece = getNextState({
210:        core,
211:        ai: undefined,
212:        piece
213:      }, 'D').piece
214:
215:      /* node:coverage disable */
216:      if (nextPiece === null) {
217:        throw Error('This should be impossible')
218:      }
219:      /* node:coverage enable */
220:
221:      piece = nextPiece
222:    }
223:
224:    const piecePositions = [piece]
225:
226:    const seen = new Set()
227:    seen.add(getHashCode(piece))
228:
229:    const possibleFutures: CoreState[] = []
230:
231:    // A simple `forEach` won't work here because we are appending to the list as we go
232:    let i = 0
233:    while (i < piecePositions.length) {
234:      piece = piecePositions[i]
235:
236:      // apply all possible moves
237:      moves.forEach(move => {
238:        const nextState = getNextState({
239:          core,
240:          ai: undefined,
241:          piece
242:        }, move)
243:        const newPiece = nextState.piece
244:
245:        if (newPiece === null) {
246:          // piece locked? better add that to the list
247:          // do NOT check locations, they aren't significant here
248:          possibleFutures.push(nextState.core)
249:        } else {
250:          // transform succeeded?
251:          // new location? append to list
252:          // check locations, they are significant
253:          const newHashCode = getHashCode(newPiece)
254:
255:          if (!seen.has(newHashCode)) {
256:            piecePositions.push(newPiece)
257:            seen.add(newHashCode)
258:          }
259:        }
260:      })
261:      i++
262:    }
263:
264:    return possibleFutures
265:  }
266:
267:  const validateAiResult = async (enemy: Enemy, coreState: CoreState, aiState: any) => {
268:    const aiResult: string | [string, any] = await enemy.ai(coreState, aiState, getNextCoreStates)
269:
270:    const [unsafePieceId, nextAiState] = Array.isArray(aiResult)
271:      ? aiResult
272:      : [aiResult, aiState]
273:
274:    if (pieceIds.includes(unsafePieceId)) {
275:      return [unsafePieceId, nextAiState]
276:    }
277:
278:    throw Error(`Bad piece ID: ${unsafePieceId}`)
279:  }
280:
281:  const getFirstWellState = async ({ enemy }: GameState): Promise<WellState> => {
282:    const firstCoreState = {
283:      well: Array(wellDepth).fill(0),
284:      score: 0
285:    }
286:
287:    const [firstPieceId, firstAiState] = await validateAiResult(enemy, firstCoreState, undefined)
288:
289:    return {
290:      core: firstCoreState,
291:      ai: firstAiState,
292:      piece: rotationSystem.placeNewPiece(wellWidth, firstPieceId)
293:    }
294:  }
295:
296:  /**
297:    Accepts the input of a move and attempts to apply that
298:    transform to the live piece in the live well.
299:    Returns the new state. Technically the new state could be partial but to
300:    satisfy the compiler make it whole
301:  */
302:  const handleMove = async (state: GameState, move: string): Promise<GameState> => {
303:    const {
304:      enemy,
305:      mode,
306:      replay,
307:      wellStateId,
308:      wellStates
309:    } = state
310:    const nextWellStateId = wellStateId + 1
311:
312:    let nextReplay
313:    let nextWellStates
314:
315:    if (wellStateId in replay && move === replay[wellStateId]) {
316:      nextReplay = replay
317:      nextWellStates = wellStates
318:    } else {
319:      // Push the new move
320:      nextReplay = replay.slice(0, wellStateId).concat([move])
321:
322:      // And truncate the future
323:      nextWellStates = wellStates.slice(0, wellStateId + 1)
324:    }
325:
326:    if (!(nextWellStateId in nextWellStates)) {
327:      const nextWellState = getNextState(nextWellStates[wellStateId], move)
328:      nextWellStates = [...nextWellStates, nextWellState]
329:    }
330:
331:    const nextWellState = nextWellStates[nextWellStateId]
332:
333:    // Is the game over?
334:    // It is impossible to get bits at row (bar - 2) or higher without getting a bit at
335:    // row (bar - 1), so there is only one line which we need to check.
336:    const gameIsOver = nextWellState.core.well[bar - 1] !== 0
337:
338:    const nextMode = gameIsOver ? 'GAME_OVER' : mode
339:
340:    // no live piece? make a new one
341:    // suited to the new world, of course
342:    if (nextWellState.piece === null && nextMode !== 'GAME_OVER') {
343:      let pieceId: string
344:      let aiState: any
345:      try {
346:        // TODO: `nextWellState.core.well` should be more complex and contain colour
347:        // information, whereas the well passed to the AI should be a simple
348:        // array of integers
349:        [pieceId, aiState] = await validateAiResult(enemy, nextWellState.core, nextWellState.ai)
350:      } catch (error_) {
351:        const error = error_ as Error
352:        console.error(error)
353:        return {
354:          ...state,
355:          error: {
356:            interpretation: 'Caught this exception while trying to generate a new piece using your custom AI. Game halted.',
357:            real: error.message,
358:            dismissable: true
359:          }
360:        }
361:      }
362:
363:      nextWellState.ai = aiState
364:      nextWellState.piece = rotationSystem.placeNewPiece(wellWidth, pieceId)
365:    }
366:
367:    return {
368:      ...state,
369:      mode: nextMode,
370:      wellStateId: nextWellStateId,
371:      wellStates: nextWellStates,
372:      replay: nextReplay
373:    }
374:  }
375:
376:  return {
377:    getFirstWellState,
378:    getNextCoreStates,
379:    handleMove
380:  }
381:}
